This is production engineering, not greenfield prototyping. The services you join already carry live traffic, real merchant data and third-party integrations that cannot break.
The defining constraint of this role is that your API is somebody else's production dependency. A breaking change is not a deploy you can roll back quietly; it is an outage in someone else's product. A year ago, we would have posted this as a backend role. That role doesn't really exist any more.
Code has become nearly invisible. Agents write it, test it, and iterate on it faster than anyone could read it. What's left is the work above it: deciding what's worth building, designing systems that hold up at 10x, and building the setup that turns a clear spec into working software.
That's the job. At your level, it isn't one system. It's several workstreams, running at once.
You'll work directly with our Cofounder/CTO on products going from zero to one, with AI at the core of both what we build and how we build it. **What you'll do**
* **Own multiple workstreams in parallel.** Two or three features of the same product moving at once, each with its own scope, edge cases, and failure modes. You decide where your attention goes this week, and nothing goes stale.

jobs.title: Builder Developer II
jobs.description:
**Job Description**

**The Builder-2 (Dev) Profile**

You are a full-stack agent engineer. You can take a complex business requirement and build the multi-step AI workflow that solves it, end to end, without someone breaking it down for you first.

**1. Core DNA**

* **AI-Native Workflow.** You use AI to accelerate development, testing and documentation as a default, not an experiment. You have opinions about which tools earn their place.
* **Agentic Implementation.** You build, debug and deploy autonomous agents (LangGraph, AutoGen, Playwright-LLM hybrids) that navigate complex ERP schemas and long-running business logic.
* **Legacy-to-Modern Bridge.** You treat 20-year-old systems as puzzles for AI-driven modernization, not as someone else’s problem.
* **Evidence Over Confidence.** You don’t ship an agent because the demo went well. You ship it because you can show what it does on the edge cases — and you know your own error rate rather than claiming there isn’t one.

**2. What You Own**

**Your agent.** Design, build, debug, deploy, and keep running. Including the unglamorous parts: retries, state recovery, timeouts, what happens when the model is down.

**The evidence it works.** Before you refactor an undocumented module, you capture what it currently does — characterization tests, real inputs, real outputs. After, you show the behaviour matches. Your Builder 3 sets the standard; meeting it is your job, not theirs.

**Your blast radius.** You know exactly what your agent is permitted to touch, and you build so a wrong answer costs a review comment rather than a bad ledger entry.

**3. Your Elective Specialty (lean into one)**

* **The Agentic Architect (Systems)** — you don’t just build APIs, you build tool-calling interfaces and state management for agentic graphs that survive long-running business processes.
* **The UX/Interaction Builder (Product)** — the chatbox is just the beginning. You build generative UIs and browser-use agents that navigate existing portals to get work done.
* **The Data & Context Engineer (Data)** — master of the RAG pipeline. Vector stores, chunking strategy, and knowledge graphs that teach the AI how a Purchase Order relates to a GL entry.
* **The Reliability & Eval Engineer (QA)** — you move the team from prompt vibes to prompt engineering. DSPy for programmatic optimization, red-teaming agents to pressure-test financial logic.
* **The Infra & Agent-Ops Builder (DevOps)** — you build the factory where agents live: tracing, logging and monitoring the thoughts of the AI.
* **The Domain Logic Translator (Business)** — you take 50 pages of accounting regulation and turn it into structured system prompts and agentic constraints.

**What You’ll Actually Do**

* **Build execution agents.** Move beyond RAG into action — agents that navigate an ERP schema, find a data discrepancy and propose the fix.
* **Automate the untestable.** Wrap legacy business logic in modern tests and documentation using AI, starting with the modules everyone else has avoided.
* **Prove parity.** Capture what the old code does before you replace it, and show the new path matches — on the boring cases and the fiscal-calendar, multi-currency, partial-shipment ones.
* **Prompt engineering and evals.** Use frameworks like DSPy to move from vibes-based prompting to programmatic, optimized instructions.
* **Rapid prototyping.** Turn a “what if” into a working AI-driven feature in days, not months.
* **Fix your own agents in production.** …

 They program robots. Agents read datasheets so our pick-and-place machines know how to handle each new part.
 They watch the factory. They spot stray parts in robot storage, diagnose printer faults and clear stuck machines.

jobs.description:
**Job Description**

**The Builder-2 (Dev) Profile**

You are a full-stack agent engineer. You can take a complex business requirement and build the multi-step AI workflow that solves it, end to end, without someone breaking it down for you first.

**1. Core DNA**

* **AI-Native Workflow.** You use AI to accelerate development, testing and documentation as a default, not an experiment. You have opinions about which tools earn their place.
* **Agentic Implementation.** You build, debug and deploy autonomous agents (LangGraph, AutoGen, Playwright-LLM hybrids) that navigate complex ERP schemas and long-running business logic.
* **Legacy-to-Modern Bridge.** You treat 20-year-old systems as puzzles for AI-driven modernization, not as someone else’s problem.
* **Evidence Over Confidence.** You don’t ship an agent because the demo went well. You ship it because you can show what it does on the edge cases — and you know your own error rate rather than claiming there isn’t one.

**2. What You Own**

**Your agent.** Design, build, debug, deploy, and keep running. Including the unglamorous parts: retries, state recovery, timeouts, what happens when the model is down.

**The evidence it works.** Before you refactor an undocumented module, you capture what it currently does — characterization tests, real inputs, real outputs. After, you show the behaviour matches. Your Builder 3 sets the standard; meeting it is your job, not theirs.

**Your blast radius.** You know exactly what your agent is permitted to touch, and you build so a wrong answer costs a review comment rather than a bad ledger entry.

**3. Your Elective Specialty (lean into one)**

* **The Agentic Architect (Systems)** — you don’t just build APIs, you build tool-calling interfaces and state management for agentic graphs that survive long-running business processes.
* **The UX/Interaction Builder (Product)** — the chatbox is just the beginning. You build generative UIs and browser-use agents that navigate existing portals to get work done.
* **The Data & Context Engineer (Data)** — master of the RAG pipeline. Vector stores, chunking strategy, and knowledge graphs that teach the AI how a Purchase Order relates to a GL entry.
* **The Reliability & Eval Engineer (QA)** — you move the team from prompt vibes to prompt engineering. DSPy for programmatic optimization, red-teaming agents to pressure-test financial logic.
* **The Infra & Agent-Ops Builder (DevOps)** — you build the factory where agents live: tracing, logging and monitoring the thoughts of the AI.
* **The Domain Logic Translator (Business)** — you take 50 pages of accounting regulation and turn it into structured system prompts and agentic constraints.

**What You’ll Actually Do**

* **Build execution agents.** Move beyond RAG into action — agents that navigate an ERP schema, find a data discrepancy and propose the fix.
* **Automate the untestable.** Wrap legacy business logic in modern tests and documentation using AI, starting with the modules everyone else has avoided.
* **Prove parity.** Capture what the old code does before you replace it, and show the new path matches — on the boring cases and the fiscal-calendar, multi-currency, partial-shipment ones.
* **Prompt engineering and evals.** Use frameworks like DSPy to move from vibes-based prompting to programmatic, optimized instructions.
* **Rapid prototyping.** Turn a “what if” into a working AI-driven feature in days, not months.
* **Fix your own agents in production.** …

You are a full-stack agent engineer. You can take a complex business requirement and build the multi-step AI workflow that solves it, end to end, without someone breaking it down for you first.

**1. Core DNA**

* **AI-Native Workflow.** You use AI to accelerate development, testing and documentation as a default, not an experiment. You have opinions about which tools earn their place.
* **Agentic Implementation.** You build, debug and deploy autonomous agents (LangGraph, AutoGen, Playwright-LLM hybrids) that navigate complex ERP schemas and long-running business logic.
* **Legacy-to-Modern Bridge.** You treat 20-year-old systems as puzzles for AI-driven modernization, not as someone else’s problem.
* **Evidence Over Confidence.** You don’t ship an agent because the demo went well. You ship it because you can show what it does on the edge cases — and you know your own error rate rather than claiming there isn’t one.

**2. What You Own**

**Your agent.** Design, build, debug, deploy, and keep running. Including the unglamorous parts: retries, state recovery, timeouts, what happens when the model is down.

**The evidence it works.** Before you refactor an undocumented module, you capture what it currently does — characterization tests, real inputs, real outputs. After, you show the behaviour matches. Your Builder 3 sets the standard; meeting it is your job, not theirs.

**Your blast radius.** You know exactly what your agent is permitted to touch, and you build so a wrong answer costs a review comment rather than a bad ledger entry.

**3. Your Elective Specialty (lean into one)**

* **The Agentic Architect (Systems)** — you don’t just build APIs, you build tool-calling interfaces and state management for agentic graphs that survive long-running business processes.

* **The Reliability & Eval Engineer (QA)** — you move the team from prompt vibes to prompt engineering. DSPy for programmatic optimization, red-teaming agents to pressure-test financial logic.
* **The Infra & Agent-Ops Builder (DevOps)** — you build the factory where agents live: tracing, logging and monitoring the thoughts of the AI.
* **The Domain Logic Translator (Business)** — you take 50 pages of accounting regulation and turn it into structured system prompts and agentic constraints.

**What You’ll Actually Do**

* **Build execution agents.** Move beyond RAG into action — agents that navigate an ERP schema, find a data discrepancy and propose the fix.
* **Automate the untestable.** Wrap legacy business logic in modern tests and documentation using AI, starting with the modules everyone else has avoided.
* **Prove parity.** Capture what the old code does before you replace it, and show the new path matches — on the boring cases and the fiscal-calendar, multi-currency, partial-shipment ones.
* **Prompt engineering and evals.** Use frameworks like DSPy to move from vibes-based prompting to programmatic, optimized instructions.
* **Rapid prototyping.** Turn a “what if” into a working AI-driven feature in days, not months.

jobs.description:
About CircuitHub CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.
 We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.
 The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.
 Overview CircuitHub is primarily built using a combination of Haskell, Nix, and PostgreSQL, deployed to both AWS and bare metal machines. We use a significant amount of open-source technology, and also try and give back where possible (for example, both Rel8 and Fast Downward Haskell bindings ).
 CircuitHub spans a vast problem space. Challenges include computer vision (OpenCV), machine learning (PyTorch), hard optimization problems (Z3/MiniZinc/OR-Tools), and all the normal engineering challenges of building both web-based customer-facing and internal tooling.
 We work on manufacturing execution systems, enterprise resource planning, and robotics. An old video from Haskell Exchange 2019 hints at what we are up to on the robotics side. We have progressed significantly since then!
 These roles are remote (any location), in-person, or hybrid, depending on preference.
 We have offices in South Deerfield - USA, Cambridge, and London, UK.
 Salary depends on the candidate and location, but as guidance in the UK, a likely range is £80k to £125k and in the US $125k to $250k, with additional equity.
 CircuitHub has raised $45M from top-tier VCs and has been going for about ten years. CircuitHub is profitable, with tens of millions in revenue. Small team (CircuitHub is ~50 employees) with tremendous growth opportunity and low risk. We are aiming to 10x capacity through 2027 in both our existing Massachusetts factory and expand into Europe.
   Team/Environment/Role Our R&D team is more than 20 people, with eight engineers working directly on the Haskell code base. We are looking to expand the team significantly this year. We have many exciting problems to solve, from robotic path planning to more conventional web products.
 We are happy to consider candidates without commercial Haskell experience, but your other skills and experience would need to compensate. A possible profile, for instance, would be a professional robotics background with some hobbyist FP experience.
 Conversely, for experienced Haskellers without experience in our domain, we will look for interests that correlate with what we are trying to accomplish. Life is too short to work on something you are not passionate about!
   Location Work remotely, or from one of our offices in the UK (London, Cambridge) or USA (Boston)

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Backend
jobs.description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 
 We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.
 We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.
 Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.
 We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.
 About the role You’ll build backend systems that make our lab programmable. You'll architect data pipelines that process large-scale protein characterization data, build APIs that integrate laboratory instruments and robotics into our software stack, and work closely with scientists and automation engineers to translate complex molecular biology workflows into reliable, scalable software. This is not SaaS slop, you're making physical machines do precise biology with minimal human intervention.
 What we're looking for 
 Strong experience designing and building production backend systems. We use Python and TypeScript on the backend with Postgres, but what matters is that you can architect systems that are reliable and maintainable.
 Experience building data pipelines and processing infrastructure. You'll be handling large volumes of heterogeneous data from physical instruments such as binding kinetics data, enzyme activity measurements, chromatography readings, and turning them into clean, structured datasets.
 Comfortable with API design and systems integration. A big part of this role is making hardware talk to software: connecting instruments, robotics, and scheduling systems into a coherent whole.
 A genuine interest in biology. No background required, but our product is running biology experiments in the physical world and that should excite you.
 High-autonomy, founder mindset. We share context and vision openly. You figure out what matters most and go work on it.
 Pragmatism. You care about solving the problem well, not about the stack or the tools.
 You write code primarily with AI, but you have enough experience writing software without it to know what good code and good architecture look like.
 
 Application deadline

**Engagement Type:** Contract-to-hire, 3 months then ongoing

**Reports to:** CEO

About MarcoPolo Learning

MarcoPolo Learning is a leading provider of innovative content, technology, and instructional support for early childhood education. Since 2013, we’ve impacted thousands of classrooms and hundreds of thousands of families across North America. Our Emmy-nominated MarcoPolo World School app and The Polos TV series bring STEM and global discovery to life for young learners.

Backed by top-tier investors, we’re on a mission to transform early learning at scale. At the center of that mission is Audrey, our AI Teaching Companion & Coach for early-learning educators.

Role Overview

We’re looking for an AI Product Engineer who builds with AI by default and cares deeply about the product. You’ll partner closely with our CEO to shape and move Audrey forward. You’ll turn ideas into clear decisions, then build them end to end alongside a small, collaborative engineering team.

This role suits someone who leads through clarity and trust, brings people with them, and helps the whole team do its best work.

Key Responsibilities

* Partner with the CEO on product direction: shape priorities, test assumptions, and turn ideas into clear, buildable plans.
* Design and build AI features end to end, including prompts and agents, retrieval, and the experience around them.

* **By 90 days:** help shape the next phase of the product roadmap with the CEO.

* 5–8 years of full-stack software engineering: React/TypeScript front end; Node.js or Python back end; AWS.

* Hands-on experience with prompt and agent design, RAG (embeddings, vector search, re-ranking), and evaluating LLM output quality.
* An AI-native way of working: you use AI tools every day and can show the speed it gives you.

Dans le cadre de l’ouverture d’un poste en CDI, nous recrutons un.e AI engineer, basé-e au choix à Lille ou Paris.

 

🚀 CONTEXTE & ENJEUX STRATÉGIQUES

Au sein de Decathlon Digital, l'équipe Finance Data engage une initiative majeure : transformer les métiers de la finance par l'intégration de l'IA Générative et Agentique.

Face à la fragmentation des analyses exécutées par la fonction FP&A, notre ambition est de construire des solutions plus standardisées avec l’appui de l’IA. Il s'agit d’implémenter des couches d'intelligence centralisées et agnostiques des outils, capable d'interagir avec l'ensemble de notre infrastructure (Workday, Data Lake, EPM, ...) pour faire évoluer nos interfaces d'une logique de consultation vers une logique d'action.

Dans ce cadre, nous développons des débriefs de performance financière générés par l’IA pour toutes les activités de l’entreprise. Il aide nos collaborateurs et managers à accéder instantanément à une information fiable et sur laquelle ils peuvent prendre des décisions.

Déjà déployé avec succès en France, Espagne, Italie et Belgique, ce projet est le premier d’une série à venir.

Pour mener ce projet, nous ne recherchons pas uniquement un.e développeur.se, nous avons besoin d'un.e "Builder" : un.e personne capable de traduire un besoin métier en solution technique, de l’implémenter, la qualifier, la déployer et la maintenir dans le temps.

 

 🎯 VOTRE MISSION

Nous recherchons un(e) AI Engineer confirmé(e) pour participer activement à l'industrialisation et au développement de nos solutions d’IA pour les contrôleurs de gestion. Votre objectif est clair : transformer les besoins métiers en fonctionnalités IA fiables, mesurables et robustes.

Pour relever ce défi, vous évoluerez au sein d'un collectif dédié, en collaboration directe avec d'autres AI Engineers et un Product Manager. Cette organisation de proximité vous permettra d'assurer une synergie parfaite entre les enjeux produits, la roadmap et l'implémentation technique.

jobs.title: Data/ML engineer, fusion data
jobs.description:
Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation, and control stack for the fusion energy reactors of the future.
 Spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and backed by top investors, our technology enables reliable operation, real-time monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices. We are founded by world-class experts at the intersection of fusion physics, advanced control, and AI (ex-Google DeepMind, EPFL). We are assembling a founding engineering team in Lausanne to build our core technology platform.
 We are looking for a Data / Machine Learning Engineer to join our team. This job is for you if you like turning large, messy, heterogeneous experimental data into clean, labelled, trustworthy datasets. You have done this with scientific or industrial sensor data. Familiarity with fusion is a plus but not a strict requirement.
 Responsibilities Build, maintain and run pipelines that bring experimental fusion data into high quality, consistent, documented, versioned datasets.
 Develop ML-assisted labelling and event detection (e.g. disruptions, MHD activity, diagnostic faults), using weak supervision, active learning and anomaly detection.
 Own data quality and provisioning: provenance, calibration metadata, automated validation. Manage and facilitate access for the rest of the team.
 Work with physicists validating the datasets & labels.
 Work with our computational scientists and control engineers, who build models and controllers on these datasets, and with customers to understand and integrate their data.
 Requirements Hands-on experience building data pipelines for large scientific or industrial time-series data formats (e.g. HDF5, Parquet, Zarr).
 Proficiency in designing, querying and optimizing SQL and noSQL database systems and familiarity with Time Series databases such as TimescaleDB, InfluxDB.
 Experience in applying ML techniques to time series in Python (PyTorch or JAX): sequence models, anomaly and event detection, semi- or weakly-supervised labelling.
 Solid software engineering habits: testing, reproducibility, data versioning are second nature to you.
 Evidence of independent work at the highest level: a PhD thesis and/or published code that is used by others, or an industry project you owned. You should be comfortable designing data architectures independently from day 1.
 The following are an advantage but not strictly required:
 Human-in-the-loop labelling tools and workflows.
 Pipeline Orchestration (e.g. Dagster, Airflow, Prefect) and data versioning (e.g. DVC, lakeFS).
 Data from large physics experiments: fusion, accelerators, astronomy, or exposure to fusion data systems (MDSplus, IMAS).
 What we offer Play a key role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up.
 Build cutting edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts.
 Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life.
 Competitive salary and equity compensation, matched to level of seniority, and benefits including immigration assistance.
